Ultra announces $50 million Series A to scale warehouse robots

The company disclosed $62 million in funding including earlier capital, with deployment and sustained operation at customer sites as its focus.

Ultra ↗9 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 3

New round versus total funding

Ultra announced $62 million in funding on October 9, including a $50 million Series A led by Framework Ventures. The total therefore should not be confused with the size of the Series A alone. The company says it spent two and a half years deploying robots with customers and learning from work on warehouse floors.

A workstation-focused product

Operator, also called OP1, targets packing, sorting and kitting. Ultra describes a stationary machine using a standard 120-volt outlet, with a roughly five-by-five-foot footprint and a payload of up to ten pounds per arm. Its service approach makes installation, support and keeping machines useful at customer sites central parts of the product, alongside robot intelligence.

What remains undisclosed

The announcement says robots are operating in American warehouses and names Manifest, Highline Commerce and ShipsaLot among early customers. It does not disclose fleet size, revenue or per-robot economics. The financing supports expansion, but does not establish that every warehouse task is automated or that all deployments produce the same returns.
